target.title: fix: macOS GUI reads launchd wrapper auth env
target.body:
Fixes #98589

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running the macOS GUI against a Node-managed local gateway could fail to authenticate when the gateway LaunchAgent stored auth in OpenClaw's generated service env file instead of inline plist `EnvironmentVariables`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The macOS LaunchAgent snapshot reader now mirrors the generated launchd wrapper shape used by the Node gateway service installer: it reads `service-env/<label>.env`, merges those values over inline plist env, and unwraps the generated wrapper arguments before deriving gateway port/bind/auth. Custom wrappers are left untouched unless they match OpenClaw's generated `service-env/<label>-env-wrapper.sh` plus `<label>.env` contract.

## User Impact

macOS GUI local-mode fallback auth can now discover gateway token/password values installed through the generated launchd service env wrapper, so GUI reconnects do not silently miss valid local gateway credentials.

## Evidence

- `swiftc -typecheck apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/Launchctl.swift apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/Process+PipeRead.swift apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/String+NonEmpty.swift apps/macos/Sources/OpenClaw/FileHandle+SafeRead.swift`
- Compiled Swift proof comparing `origin/main` against this branch with the same temporary generated LaunchAgent plist and env file.
- `git diff --check`
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local`

### Real behavior proof

#### Behavior addressed

The macOS GUI launchd snapshot path missed `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN` and `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PASSWORD` when Node launchd installed them through OpenClaw's generated `service-env/<label>.env` wrapper file.

#### Environment

Local macOS Swift compiler proof in this repository branch, using a temporary generated LaunchAgent plist with:

- `ProgramArguments`: `service-env/ai.openclaw.gateway-env-wrapper.sh`, `service-env/ai.openclaw.gateway.env`, then `openclaw gateway --port 18789 --bind loopback`
- Inline plist env: `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN=inline-token`
- Generated env file: `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_TOKEN=' file-token '` and `OPENCLAW_GATEWAY_PASSWORD='file-password'`

#### Current-main contrast

The same proof compiled against `origin/main` showed the bug:

```text
mode=base
programArguments=/var/.../service-env/ai.openclaw.gateway-env-wrapper.sh /var/.../service-env/ai.openclaw.gateway.env openclaw gateway --port 18789 --bind loopback
token=inline-token
password=nil
envToken=inline-token
envPassword=nil
```

#### Exact steps or command run after this patch

Compiled the current branch's `Launchctl.swift` with its local dependencies and executed the same generated LaunchAgent plist/env-file proof scenario.

#### Evidence after fix

```text
mode=head
programArguments=openclaw gateway --port 18789 --bind loopback
token=file-token
password=file-password
envToken= file-token 
envPassword=file-password
```

#### Evidence artifact links

Local proof logs from this run:

- `/tmp/openclaw-launchd-real-proof.h68H9I/base.log`
- `/tmp/openclaw-launchd-real-proof.h68H9I/head.log`

#### Control check

A custom wrapper ending in `-env-wrapper.sh` but not matching OpenClaw's generated `service-env/<label>-env-wrapper.sh` plus `<label>.env` shape remains wrapped and continues to use inline plist env.

#### Observed result after fix

The generated launchd wrapper arguments are unwrapped to `openclaw gateway --port 18789 --bind loopback`, and file-backed gateway token/password values are available to the macOS snapshot consumer.

#### What was not tested

`swift test --package-path apps/macos --filter GatewayLaunchAgentManagerTests` could not complete locally because SwiftPM repeatedly fetched `https://github.com/steipete/Peekaboo.git`; the first attempt failed with an HTTP/2 RPC cancel, and later fetch attempts stalled before package tests could start.

AI-assisted change: this fix and PR body were prepared with Codex assistance; behavior proof above is from commands run against the local repository.
